headline: Measles outbreak claims 918 lives in Bangladesh; 3 more children die with symptoms
summary: Bangladesh's health ministry has struggled to contain a prolonged measles outbreak, leading to 918 deaths despite a nationwide vaccination campaign. Experts cite vaccination gaps and inadequate infection control.
details: A prolonged measles outbreak in Bangladesh has claimed 918 lives, with three more children dying with measles-like symptoms in the last 24 hours, according to the DGHS. This ongoing crisis has raised questions about the health ministry's capacity to fulfill its ambitious healthcare promises.

The ministry launched a nationwide vaccination campaign from April 5 after the disease began spreading rapidly in mid-March. However, shortcomings in target-setting and healthcare management response have failed to bring the disease under control.

Health experts, including Prof Be-Nazir Ahmed, attribute the continued spread to gaps in vaccination coverage, affecting around 40 lakh children. Infections among children outside the campaign's target age group and inadequate infection prevention measures are also contributing factors.

The emergency measles inoculation drive vaccinated 1.84 crore children by May 20. Yet, a significant coverage gap of 38.83 lakh children was exposed when compared to those who received Vitamin A capsules during a separate campaign.

State Minister of Health and Family Welfare MA Muhit maintains that the government was largely successful in containing the outbreak due to a quick response. He stated the crisis was inherited from previous governments, citing disrupted routine immunization and vaccine shortages since 2020.

Muhit acknowledged using outdated UNICEF figures for estimates and assured steps are being taken to vaccinate all missing children. He expressed hope that the outbreak would end within three months, while the ministry received its highest-ever allocation of Tk 69,409 crore for fiscal 2026-27.

However, Prof Be-Nazir noted that despite the increased budget, the health sector saw no significant progress in the government's first six months. He criticized key appointments based on political consideration rather than merit, a point partially acknowledged by Muhit.

Plans to upgrade all upazila health complexes to 151 beds were described as ambitious by experts. They warned that expanding bed capacity without addressing acute shortages of doctors, nurses, and health workers could render many upgraded facilities ineffective.

Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain vowed to ensure timely doctor attendance and took action against some clinics. Yet, experts like Prof Be-Nazir argue these visits did not significantly improve treatment quality, citing instances like the closure and reopening of Ad-din Medical College Hospital.

Muhit, however, believes their efforts and frequent visits have helped restore some public confidence in the health system. He claims the situation in hospitals is somewhat better now, particularly regarding doctor attendance.

headline_marked: Khulna: [[Youth killed in mob beating]] over child-lifter suspicion
headline: Khulna: Youth killed in mob beating over child-lifter suspicion
summary: A young man was beaten to death by a crowd in Khulna after being suspected of kidnapping children.
details: A youth was killed after being subjected to a mob beating in Khulna. The attack occurred after the victim was suspected of being a child-lifter.
The incident sparked panic and tension in the local area as a crowd gathered and attacked the man based on suspicion.
The victim was subsequently taken to the hospital, where he was declared dead.
Local authorities are investigating the incident to determine the facts and identify those involved in the mob violence.
